**Hello, I’m [Your Name], a clinician who specializes in supporting new mothers with postpartum mental‑health concerns.**  

I’d like to invite you to complete the **Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS)** today. This brief, ten‑item questionnaire helps us understand how you’ve been feeling over the past week, so we can identify any signs of depression or anxiety that sometimes arise after birth.  

Everything you share is completely confidential, and this is a safe, non‑judgmental space. My goal is simply to listen, learn about your experience, and work together to support your well‑being.  

We’ll go through the ten questions one at a time, and you can answer as honestly as you feel comfortable. If at any point something feels upsetting, just let me know and we can pause.  

When you’re ready, we can start with the first question:

**1. Over the past week, how often have you felt able to laugh or see the funny side of things?**
I’ve noticed that I’m not laughing as much as I used to. It feels like I can only see the funny side of things “only some of the time” these days.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things
Yes, I’ve only been able to laugh or see the funny side of things “some of the time” over the past week.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things
I’ve been looking forward to things “rather less than I used to” over the past week.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong
I’ve blamed myself unnecessarily “not very often” when things went wrong over the past week.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason
I’ve felt anxious or worried “sometimes” over the past week, even when there isn’t an obvious reason.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason
I’ve felt scared or panicky for no very good reason “sometimes” over the past week.
Things have been getting on top of me
I’ve felt that things have been getting on top of me “sometimes” over the past week.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping
I’ve been so unhappy that I’ve had difficulty sleeping “sometimes” over the past week.
I have felt sad or miserable
I’ve felt sad or miserable “sometimes” over the past week.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying
I’ve been crying “hardly ever” over the past week.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
I haven’t had any thoughts of harming myself “never” over the past week.

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 12: **Postpartum Mood & Anxiety Screening – Summary**

**Client Identifier:** [Name/ID]  
**Date of Screening:** [Date]  
**Screening Tool:** Self‑report symptom checklist (past week)

| Domain | Reported Frequency | Clinical Note |
|--------|--------------------|---------------|
| **Positive affect / enjoyment** | “Some of the time” able to laugh or see the funny side; “rather less than I used to” looking forward to things | Diminished pleasure and anticipatory enjoyment noted. |
| **Self‑blame / guilt** | “Not very often” blaming self unnecessarily | Minimal guilt reported. |
| **Anxiety / worry** | “Sometimes” feeling anxious or worried without obvious reason | Intermittent anxiety present. |
| **Panic / fear** | “Sometimes” feeling scared or panicky without clear trigger | Occasional panic‑type symptoms. |
| **Overwhelm / coping** | “Sometimes” feeling things are getting on top of me | Variable sense of being overwhelmed. |
| **Sleep disturbance linked to mood** | “Sometimes” difficulty sleeping because of unhappiness | Sleep impact noted, though not pervasive. |
| **Sadness / low mood** | “Sometimes” feeling sad or miserable | Mild‑moderate low mood present. |
| **Crying** | “Hardly ever” crying | Low frequency of tearful episodes. |
| **Suicidal ideation** | “Never” having thoughts of self‑harm | No current suicidal ideation. |

**Key Patterns & Findings**  
- Consistent reports of **reduced positive affect** (laughing, looking forward to activities) and **intermittent low mood** (“sometimes” sad, occasional sleep difficulty).  
- **Anxiety‑related symptoms** (worry, fear/panic, feeling overwhelmed) are present at a moderate frequency (“sometimes”).  
- **Guilt/self‑blame** is minimal.  
- No evidence of **persistent crying** or **suicidal thoughts**.

**Screening Significance for Post‑partum Depression / Anxiety**  
- **Loss of pleasure / anhedonia** and **low mood** are core features of postpartum depression.  
- **Sleep disturbance** linked to mood may reflect depressive symptomatology.  
- **Anxiety, worry, and occasional panic** are common comorbidities in the postpartum period.  
- **Absence of self‑harm ideation** reduces immediate safety concerns.

**Risk Factor Summary**  
- **Persistent sadness & reduced enjoyment:** present, though not continuous.  
- **Sleep difficulty related to mood:** reported intermittently.  
- **Feelings of being overwhelmed:** intermittent.  
- **Self‑blame/guilt:** low.  
- **Suicidal thoughts:** none reported.

**Safety & Follow‑up Recommendations** *(for clinical team)*  
- Continue routine monitoring of mood, sleep, and anxiety symptoms.  
- Re‑assess for any escalation in frequency/intensity of depressive or anxiety symptoms at next visit or sooner if changes occur.  
- Maintain open channel for the client to report emergent suicidal ideation or worsening self‑harm thoughts.

**Signature & Date:** _______________________
